Change has been successfully rebased and submitted as 3124782739408b77dbf7df07833336ee63dcc239
review this logic, it works but it looks goofy, this can probably be simplified.

In practice, this step curve is a bit jumpy, probably put Verify and Apply 98 and 100. With large disparities between total components, this pretty much jumps between 67 and 100 faster than you can get a redfish call in from bmcweb's perspective.
look into just making one UpdateProgress per device and basing it off the total component length, when the last component is in verify and apply, finish off the percentage. This is a bit complicated.
nit, consistently put in cpp or hpp, don't split.
nit, using above could make this easier to read.
we probably want to cache this, if we're not already inside of this call.
Can you elaborate on the issues here?
Can you share more details on testing (D-Bus/Redfish snippets) related to progress percentage?
How did we come up with these constants? Can we add some comments here?

sure. it was by monitoring firmware update so that it was relatively constant progress, nothing magic here. This assumes that for larger transfers, the component transfer portion will be the majority of update time, which was true in my tests.
going to be addressed in followup per discussion offline.
Why do we need to pass the eid? All these components belong to the same device so eid should be same?
Do we need any corner case checks here?
what did you have in mind. We're already checking that we're not dividing by zero above.
How is each entry associated with a specific component?
by order of component, using the existing method of tracking which component is being transferred, index.

Isn’t this too granular? Feels like we’re spamming the task.

++ @deepak.kodihalli.83@gmail.com for feedback

To clarify my concerns further- 
1. We are creating too many D-Bus logs with this change.
2. It will be difficult to interpret meaningful information from the task because these new logs will flood the task. (There’s a plan to add different update message registries to the firmware update task to provide meaningful firmware update information)
3. we should verify if these computations impact pldm CPU usage. The effect may be negligible on platforms with fewer devices, but platforms with a lot devices could see issues.

I'll wait for deepak, but it seems easier to avoid flaky updates by just reporting 0-100 rather that try to guess what is granular enough on any given firmware update. 100 dbus calls across a firmware update doesn't seem terribly unreasonable.

Can we get some data to show there's no impact to FW update perf/CPU usage with this change? That should tell us about 1 and 3.

2 - do we have some kind of limit here that you are concerned about @ranjan.rajeev1609@gmail.com? We also have severity to filter out things.

just ran a test:
PLDMd CPU usage was largely dominated by servicing pldm messages during fw update:
1. it peaked in the beginning of firmware update where we were updating all devices (CX8s, GPUs, SMAs). It peaked and sustained at around 12% of ast2600 CPU.
2. the GPUs and SMAs dropped off early (smaller firmware sizes)
3. The CPU dropped to around 2% compared to ~1% idle usage through the end of firmware update.

I would say that the 101 or so dbus calls distributed across more than five minutes are pretty negligible CPU wise.

My main concern was the task logs getting flooded. We can revisit this when we add meaningful message registries so users see more useful task information.

Also, what is the maximum CPU usage without your changes at the beginning of the firmware update? Do we have that data?

Also these progress percent changes aren’t D-Bus logs, we can ignore the comment which I had put earlier.
the same as with this change, within whole percentage points. 12 percent at the peak, tailing off as devices complete updating.
Drive by comment. Always best if you Gerrit Name matches your CCLA / Signed-off name. :) I know some maintainers enforce
Changed. Thanks, I didn't know that.
shouldn't we set to 100 after sending Activate firmware ? (we should reserve 100% for truly complete state)

We are updating progress here and not the state -> should we rename the method ?

Or shall we update the currentState to nextState here ?
yeah good catch, this should set the state at the bottom.

Should the return type of reportFwUpdate be boolean or void? 

void seems appropriate since failures are logged internally and callers can continue regardless.
sure, I'm fine with it returning void.

Accumulating into uint64_t but storing result in uint32_t here 
-> we can use const uint64_t totalSize instead
sure, we can't be larger than uint32_t since thats all the pldm package supports, but we can make both uint64_t.
Can we use one loop for calculating both totalSize and weightedProgress instead of two ?
we can, the performance hit of iterating over a vector twice versus once is going be negligable, and this seemed easier to read, but if you prefer combining this into one for loop, I can do that.
nit- (const auto& lhs, const auto& rhs)
I've been given the exact opposite feedback in other places. I'll make a using directive for this verbose type.
